classification_classes.treatment: Apply sulfur or myclobutanil early in the spring. Clear fallen leaf debris to prevent fungal ascospore overwintering.
Prune out dead or diseased wood. Spray captan or thiophanate-methyl starting from petal fall through harvest.
Eradicate nearby red cedar / juniper galls if feasible. Apply preventative sterol inhibitor fungicides.
Continue standard irrigation, canopy management, and integrated pest monitoring.
Deploy rust-tolerant hybrids. If pustules appear before tasseling, consider azoxystrobin/propiconazole application.
Rotate crops with non-grasses. Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides if lesions spread to the ear leaf during pollination.
Maintain balanced nitrogen/phosphorus supply and optimize plant population density.
Apply mancozeb or ziram starting when shoots reach 1-3 inches. Remove mummified berries from trellises.
Sanitize pruning shears. Avoid large pruning wounds in wet weather; seal cuts with wound protectant fungicides.
Continue canopy hedging to ensure adequate cluster aeration and sunlight penetration.
Apply copper hydroxide mixed with mancozeb. Avoid overhead irrigation and work only when leaves are dry.
Maintain steady drip fertigation and ensure uniform soil moisture to avoid blossom end rot.
Maintain balanced potassium and nitrogen. Apply chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin upon initial target-spot detection.
High urgency: Destroy infected foliage immediately. Apply mandipropamid, cyazofamid, or fluopicolide promptly.
Monitor canopy for early signs of blight and maintain standard hilling practices.
Prune lower 12 inches of foliage. Apply copper octanoate or difenoconazole spray on a 7-10 day schedule.
Urgent phytosanitary intervention: Isolate row and spray translaminar oomycete fungicides (mefenoxam or fluopicolide).
Lower greenhouse relative humidity below 85% via horizontal ventilation fans. Apply preventative biofungicide.
Mulch soil around plants to block spore splashing. Remove spotted bottom leaves and apply copper fungicide.
Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) or apply horticultural neem oil/insecticidal soap on undersides of leaves.
Vector control: Control whitefly populations with systemic imidacloprid or insect nets. Rogue out infected stunt plants.
Optimal physiological status. Maintain automated drip schedule and scout weekly.
